title: Constructing interval variables via faceted Rasch measurement and multitask deep learning: a hate speech application

bias_targets.methodology: Estimating the survey interpretation bias (rater severity) of human labelers using faceted Rasch item response theory (IRT) to debias the crowdsourced annotations and create an objective, continuous hate speech score.

Measuring the severity of hate speech, hostility, and bias directed at racial and ethnic groups in social media comments using a 10-item labeling instrument scaled via Rasch measurement and predicted via multitask deep learning.
Evaluating hateful and biased speech targeted at religious groups using a theorized continuous hate speech spectrum and RoBERTa-based transformer models.
Assessing hostility, dehumanization, and bias directed at different gender identities using crowdsourced annotations transformed into an interval variable.
Detecting and measuring hate speech severity against various sexual orientations using a multitask neural architecture trained on debiased annotator ratings.
Measuring hate speech and biased text directed at specific nationalities, immigrants, or undocumented persons using deep natural language processing and dynamic slur tagging.
Identifying hate speech targeted at individuals with physical, cognitive, or mental health disabilities via a multi-component crowdsourced survey.
Evaluating biased and hateful speech directed at specific age cohorts (e.g., children, seniors) using text analysis and continuous interval scaling.
